I will start from what has worked for me before and only move a little. On 9 mu, I cannot gamble. If cotton fails, the whole year feels bad, so I will still put most of my land into cotton because that is the crop I count on. I do have a well, so I am not as scared of a dry spell as some others, and that lets me spend a bit more on fertilizer and water. I never like cutting fertilizer too hard. Losing yield costs more than wasting a little bag of fertilizer. For wheat and maize, I will keep smaller areas and manage them the way people around me do when they want a steady harvest: enough base fertilizer, one or two top dressings, water at the key time, and sprays when insects or disease show up. I learned by doing, so I will not make fancy changes. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen it work in nearby fields, but I will still farm in the old practical way: plough before the season, put real fertilizer in, irrigate on time, and do not wait too long on pests.
